title: There's a Crayfish as Heavy as a Bowling Ball (and It Lives 40 Years)

scenes.text: There's a crayfish as heavy as a bowling ball.
It lives in Tasmania. 80 centimetres long, 5 kilograms. The biggest freshwater invertebrate on Earth.
Scientists just crowned North America's biggest crayfish. Its body measured under 9 centimetres.
The Tasmanian giant grows slowly. It can live 40 years, and females don't breed until they're 14.
That slow life nearly wiped it out. Catching one has been illegal since 1998.
A crayfish as heavy as a bowling ball, and older than most people watching this.

description:
There's a crayfish as heavy as a bowling ball.
The Tasmanian giant freshwater crayfish grows up to 80 centimetres and 5 kilograms, the largest freshwater invertebrate in the world. It can live around 40 years and females only start breeding at about 14, which is why it is threatened and fully protected since 1998. A new study in the journal Ecology just crowned North America's biggest crayfish, with a body under 9 centimetres.
Would you pick one up? Comment below.
thumbnail_text: A CRAYFISH HEAVY AS A BOWLING BALL
first_comment: Bonus: in Tasmania they call it a lobster, even though it lives in rivers. Would you pick up a 5 kilogram crayfish with your bare hands?
